Self-Host Weekly (2 October 2026)

Where we're going, we don't need Windows.

SPONSORED BY    Infisical
Self-Host Weekly is sponsored by Infisical. Self-host Infisical to manage secrets and certificates in one open-source platform. Stop chasing expired certificates and scattered secrets. Try Infisical for free!

Weekly Highlights

Happy Friday! Last week's puzzle launch was a resounding success (over 2,000 completions!), but I also received a ton of helpful feedback from some who found it confusing. To help, I've since added a hint system and more robust instructions on how to play (check it out below!).

I've also been working on a system for tagging vibe coded projects, something many of you have been very vocal about since the AI-assisted tags were dropped from the newsletter a few weeks ago.

Unfortunately – like everything else – the topic is incredibly nuanced:

  • Most projects are using AI in some capacity, and too many readers were mistaking AI-assisted for vibe coded when evaluating the software lists below
  • I don't have the capacity to correctly identify every project – there are simply too many submissions, and sometimes it's not obvious (some devs use AI for their READMEs but not code, etc.)
  • Some readers want to see popular vibe coded projects – not because they're going to deploy them, but because they can be inspirational for their own personal projects

I think I've come up with a decent solution to address all of the above, but I'm still ironing out the kinks. Thanks for your patience in the meantime.

In actual news and activity:

  • An eagle-eyed Home Assistant user noticed a PR that merges the current community store plugin (HACS) into an official system integration called Marketplace
  • A wild Pinchflat-ngx has appeared – a fork of the popular YouTube video downloader project Pinchflat, which hasn't seen any activity in ~10 months (and if the Pokémon reference was too much of a tease for you, check this out)
  • Gitea pulled a Java and dropped the '1.' from its versioning, jumping straight from v1.27.3 to v28.0.0
  • Nostalgex, a retro cable-like experience for media servers that launched a few months ago, has officially been open sourced
  • Raspberry Pi announced they're increasing prices for certain models (again)
  • Nextcloud launched an online academy aimed at users looking to build their own Nextcloud apps
  • Unraid and 45HomeLab announced their second hardware collaboration – a smaller prebuilt server they're calling the X4
  • The developer of Pocket ID (authentication) is looking for user feedback on its interface
  • WSL containers (Linux containers on Windows) are now generally available
  • The Dutch government has officially developed its own flavor of NixOS amid growing concerns over U.S. tech reliance (joining France, Switzerland, and a growing chunk of Europe)

Happy selfh.st/ing!

Content Spotlight

Meet Tagr, a self-hosted music metadata and tag editor. Designed as a browser-based alternative to popular desktop apps, Tagr offers an intuitive web interface that can be used to browse, edit, and manage audio file tags from just about anywhere. Features include support for editing 40+ metadata fields, custom metadata, album art management, star ratings, track/disc numbering, barcodes, and a read-only display of audio file properties (codec, bitrate, etc.).

Tagr can be easily deployed via Docker and doesn't require additional containers.
